Commits last processed offset instead of next offset; stalls on offset gaps
get_committable_offsets returns the highest processed offset N, and _commit_loop passes it straight to commit_function. Arroyo commit positions mean the next offset to consume (Message.committable is offset+1), so committing N leaves the already-processed message N as the resume point. The scan in get_committable_offsets also requires every integer from last_committed+1 upward to be in all_offsets. Any offset that is never submitted, such as a compaction or transaction-marker gap, makes the scan break there, and commit

Commits last processed offset instead of next offset (off by one)
get_committable_offsets returns the highest fully processed offset, and _commit_loop passes that straight to commit_function. Arroyo commit callbacks expect the next offset to consume (BrokerValue.committable is offset+1). The tracker never adds one. So the committed position always points at an already processed message. The same value is stored as last_committed.
After a restart or rebalance, the last processed message of every partition is consumed and processed again. Uptime results can be handled twice.

It then asserts stats["total_items"] > 0. get_stats() sums qsize(), and qsize() drops as soon as a worker calls get(). If the workers drain all 10 items between the last submit and get_stats(), the count is 0 and the assertion fails. Nothing in the test blocks the workers from running first. comment_verdicts.text:
Async legacy writes inherit the request context, which is cancelled when the handler returns
Create, Delete, Update and DeleteCollection now run the legacy write in a goroutine. Each goroutine derives its timeout context from the request `ctx` with `context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...)`. The handler returns right after starting the goroutine, so the request context is cancelled and the derived context is cancelled with it. The legacy call then runs with an already-cancelled or soon-cancelled context. The goroutine also uses `obj`, `objInfo` and `options` after the handler has returned, so the ca

Storage and legacy duration metrics are mixed up
When Storage.Create or Storage.Update fails, the code calls `recordLegacyDuration(true, ...)`, which is the legacy metric. The DeleteCollection goroutine times the legacy call but reports it with `recordStorageDuration`.
Storage failures are counted as legacy errors. Legacy DeleteCollection results are counted as storage results. Dashboards and alerts built on these metrics are wrong.

Delete records the object name as the metric kind label
The success path calls `recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, ...)`. Every other call passes `options.Kind` for that argument. Delete also calls `klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log)` instead of the enriched `log`, so the downstream logger loses the name, kind and method values.
Metric label cardinality grows with every deleted object name, and delete metrics are split across labels that don't match the other methods. Logs from lower layers lack the request fields.

judge_pairs.reason: Both say recordLegacyDuration is wrongly called when Storage operation fails, instead of recordStorageDuration.
Both say Delete passes the object name instead of options.Kind to the metrics recording.
Both say Delete uses klog.NewContext with d.Log instead of the enriched log variable, losing name, kind and method values.
